chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Senani al-Mokattib (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qat'tan quoted Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, on the authority of Tamim ibn Buhlool, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Fazl al-Hashemi that Aba Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:

Of the following three I do not really know which one is a greater offense than the others. The first is following a funeral procession without having on one’s robe. The second is striking one’s buttocks with the hand at times of calamities. The third one is saying ‘Be benign to him. Have mercy upon him. May God have mercy upon you’ when attending a funeral procession.
ai.seo_question: What are the three major offenses or etiquette violations during a funeral procession according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies three specific behaviors during funeral processions that constitute significant moral offenses or lack of proper etiquette: walking behind the deceased without wearing a robe (indicating casualness or lack of solemnity), striking the thigh with the hand (a gesture of grief or impatience), and verbally urging others to be gentle and merciful to the deceased. These actions highlight the importance of dignified conduct and sincere remembrance of the dead in Shia tradition. This narration, found in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, underscores the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) in public mourning, distinguishing between genuine reverence and performative or careless gestures.
